false_success_traps: A page that says "you're not done" or tells you to check your inbox is only the first step. The emailed form still has to be completed.
An "are you human" page is not a confirmation.
The final confirmation page is not a removal. In one run the broker later sent an email declining the request, saying the privacy law it relies on did not apply in the person's state.
The old /removal address now shows a "page could not be found" error under the normal site header. That is not a form and not a confirmation.
genuine_confirmation: After you submit the form opened from the emailed link, a confirmation page says the request was received, submitted, or is processing, and an email confirms receipt. The final answer is the later email that gives the result.
name: AdvancedBackgroundChecks

opt_out_url_check.note: This page loads and shows the opt-out request form (seen again in a browser on 2026-11-16, with no bot check). The older address ending in /removal, which this project's automation uses, now returns a "page could not be found" error. The site's "Do Not Sell or Share" notice links to the address recorded here.

steps: Say whether you are the person the request is about or an authorized agent.
On the opt-out form, fill in your first name, last name, and email address. A middle name box is there too, and you can leave it empty.

The text above Submit says pressing it agrees to the site's terms and to getting emails from it. Get the user's go-ahead for that. Complete the "are you human" check if one appears, then press Submit.
The page tells you to check your inbox. You are not done yet.
Open the email and click the link within 24 hours. After that you must ask for a new link.
Fill in the opt-out form the link opens. Fill in every part accurately. Another "are you human" check may appear.
Submit the form. A confirmation page says the request was received, and an email confirms it.
Wait for a second email with the result. The broker says this comes within 45 days.
